How do I track the cards I own?

  1. Find a card by scanning it in the app or searching by name, set and full number.
  2. Confirm its printing, language and finish. Select the raw condition or enter its existing slab grade.
  3. Record the quantity and add the holding to Portfolio. Use folders to organize owned cards; keep wanted cards in the separate Wishlist.
  4. Review the available prices and history for your holdings. Check the record and price context when a value changes.

Do not add a suggested card until its printing matches. A card can have a catalog record without a published price; missing data does not mean it is worth zero. Portfolio value uses available price data and is not a guaranteed sale amount. Website Saved references do not add holdings to the app.

A collection becomes useful when it becomes a portfolio

A list can tell you that a card exists in a box. A collection tracker answers the financial question behind that list: what the confirmed holdings are worth together.

Cards enter through scan or catalog search. After you confirm the printing and grading state, their available current prices contribute to the portfolio total. The total is a reference for the holdings with available prices, not a complete appraisal when data is missing.

Valuation keeps each holding distinct

  • Each entry is linked to a catalog card with its set and card number
  • Finish and language are confirmed when the entry is added
  • Raw copies carry their condition; graded copies carry the grading company and grade
  • Identical copies can use quantity, while different conditions, finishes, languages or grades remain distinct entries

Price history explains the portfolio movement

A current total is only the latest point. Card AI keeps available price history on individual cards, so you can separate a collection-wide move from one valuable holding changing sharply.

That makes the page a portfolio tracker rather than another catalog view: it is organized around value, contribution, and change over time.

Keep a set checklist separate from your holdings

A checklist shows which numbered cards belong to a set. Your collection records which copies you own, including quantity, finish, language and condition or existing slab grade. A full set's reference value is not the value of your personal holdings.

Use the public Ascended Heroes card list, Chaos Rising card list or Phantasmal Flames card list to check a numbered entry, then add the confirmed copy in the Card AI app. The Pokemon card value guides help separate selected printings before you save them. These public lists do not read your account or mark cards as owned.

Card collection tracker questions.

What should a card collection tracker app keep separate?

It should keep distinct printings, finishes, languages, raw conditions and existing slab grades as distinct holdings. Card AI links each entry to a confirmed catalog record, while the digital card binder handles inventory search and organization.

Can I track duplicates of the same card?

Yes. Copies are stored as separate entries, distinguished by condition, finish, language and grade, so two copies of the same card in different states are tracked and valued independently.

Does the collection value update on its own?

Yes. The total reflects current market prices for the printings you own and moves as those prices change, rather than holding the value from when you added the card.

Can I add cards without scanning them?

Yes. Search the card catalog by name, set or card number and add a matching record directly.

Can I use this as a Pokemon card collection tracker?

Yes. Filter the collection to Pokemon, keep each confirmed printing and condition or grade distinct, and follow the available price history and portfolio value for the cards you own.

Is this a card collection app or a collection manager?

Both descriptions fit. As a card collector app it catalogs what you own; as a collection manager it tracks condition, grade, quantity and value per entry. The distinction matters less than whether the records are tied to real printings, which they are.

How is card collection value calculated?

The total combines available published prices for your confirmed holdings and quantities, using each printing and its condition or existing grade. Missing prices are unavailable, not zero, so the total is not a complete appraisal or guaranteed sale amount.

Does it work as a TCG collector app for a single game?

Yes. The collection filters by game, so it works as a TCG collection app for one supported title or as a single tracker across supported TCG and sports-card categories.

Does a set checklist show which cards I own?

No. A checklist describes a release; your app holdings record the copies and quantities you own.
